Guard

Network/application protection

Filter inbound and outbound traffic across all network layers.

1. Core Concept

  • Network protection works in layers. The edge absorbs massive attacks and HTTP exploits. Subnets block IP ranges. Security Groups act as stateful firewalls for individual resources.

2. Key Services & Features

  • Security Groups:
    • Tied to ENIs/Instances.
    • Stateful (return traffic is automatically allowed).
    • Default deny all inbound. ONLY Allow rules.
  • Network ACLs (NACLs):
    • Tied to Subnets.
    • Stateless (must explicitly allow return traffic on ephemeral ports).
    • Evaluated in number order. Supports Deny rules.
  • AWS WAF:
    • Layer 7 HTTP/S firewall.
    • Attaches to ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway.
    • Blocks SQL injection, XSS, and implements rate-limiting.
  • AWS Shield:
    • DDoS protection.
    • Standard is free and automatic.
    • Advanced provides 24/7 expert response and scaling cost protection.

3. Architecture Rules

  • Chain Security Groups: A database SG should allow inbound traffic only from the Application SG, not from an IP range.
  • Use NACLs to explicitly block known malicious IPs globally.
  • Always account for ephemeral ports (1024-65535) when writing NACL outbound rules.

4. Scenarios & Use Cases

  • Block a specific IP address that is flooding your network.
    • Choose: Network ACL (NACL).
    • Why: Security Groups do not support 'Deny' rules.
  • Protect a public-facing API from SQL injection and rate-limit aggressive callers.
    • Choose: AWS WAF.
    • Why: It inspects HTTP request payloads (Layer 7) where these attacks occur.

  • B AWS WAF only
  • C AWS Shield Advanced
  • D AWS IAM Access Analyzer
Answer: C

Shield Advanced adds enhanced detection, response support, and DDoS cost protection.
